transcript: Have you ever wondered what it would be like if Brooke Dubek and Joel Maisel went on a date? Well, that is the plot of Strategic Love play, a new play starring Helena Yorke from the other two and Michael Zegen from the Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, among others. This play is an exploration on love and modern dating in the age of dating apps. And the basic premise is that these two are on a date when Helena's character suggests, what if we just gave up? What if we just end up together because we're tired of dating? And this is something that anyone who has been single for an extended period of time can probably relate to. That feeling of just going on an endless string of first dates that never seem to go anywhere, and then going back to the apps and just swiping, swiping, swiping, and how impersonal that whole process can feel. So you totally understand why these characters would come to this conclusion. And at certain points in the show, you're either rooting for it and saying, wait, this is actually a good idea, and at other points you're rooting against it and you're like, this is a terrible idea. And so I thought it was a really interesting thought experiment, and it was a play that I think will leave you with a lot to discuss afterwards. I also thought the performances by both actors was really strong, especially Michael, who really impressed me. But it was really nice to have Helene York back on a stage again, and she really is such a gifted comedic actress. Overall, I really enjoyed Strategic Love Play. I think the themes and topics that it explores are really interesting, and I thought the performances were great. So definitely check it out if you can. It is running at the Audible Theater through December 7th, so it's a super short run, but if you have time to squeeze it in, you're looking to get existential about your love life, this is the play for you.
